answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must call MSHA within 15 minutes, once the operator knows or should know that the accident has occurred. The rule covers a death of an individual at the mine.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once it knows or should know an accident has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the covered accidents.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. It rises only where methane is present.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The percentage is increased only where methane is present in a ventilating current (0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane).
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each underground miner must be given an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Under 30 CFR 57.4361, an underground metal or nonmetal mine must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift, at a time other than a shift change.

claims.text: Underground mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. The training must be conducted in conditions that duplicate actual underground conditions as closely as practicable. About 8 of the 40 hours must be given at the minesite.

claims.text: A new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training must be conducted in conditions that duplicate actual underground conditions as closely as practicable, and about 8 hours must be given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA. This is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. The same wording appears in the standards for surface mines (56.9300) and underground mines (57.9300).

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway (30 CFR 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 30 CFR 57.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. (The ERP stocking rule allows 48 hours only if advance arrangements are made for additional supplies.)

claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plans. They cover only MSHA respirable dust control plans and respiratory protection.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say. They cover MSHA mine slope, shaft and bucket rules, not OSHA construction trench requirements.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site. They cover MSHA training and records and mine map certification. They say nothing about FAA rules or drones.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design plans and permits for mining under bodies of water, and neither topic is about EPA stormwater permits.
